bibl.title: Auditory Thalamocortical Synaptic Transmission In Vitro

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: To facilitate an understanding of auditory thalamocortical mechanisms, we have developed a mouse brain-slice preparation with a functional connection between the ventral division of the medial geniculate (MGv) and the primary auditory cortex (ACx).

span.label: auditory thalamocortical synaptic transmission
span.quote: Despite a large number of anatomical and physiological studies, very little is known about the cellular and synaptic mechanisms by which thalamic inputs are transmitted to, and processed in, ACx.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Recordings took place in an interface chamber (Haas model, Med Systems) maintained at 34°C, with a liberal flow of warmed humidified gas (95% O2-5% CO2) and ACSF passing over the slices.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Thalamic glutamatergic axons excite cortical inhibitory interneurons, which then synapse on the recorded cell, producing the disynaptic fast IPSP
span.quote: Instead, it is likely that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical inhibitory interneurons to fire and those interneurons synapsed on the recorded cells, producing the IPSPs (discussed in Castro-Alamancos and Connors 1997; Douglas and Martin 1991; Porter et al. 2001).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Antidromic activation of layer 5 corticotectal cells whose axons cross the shell stimulation site, feeding back through their intracortical collaterals to generate the layer 1 sink
span.note: status: the paper's own words: it is possible that
span.quote: Thus it is possible that antidromic activation of these cells could contribute to the synaptic CSD sinks observed in the shell slice, via contacts made by their axon collaterals.

span.label: The alternative explanation for the shell slice layer 1 sink (antidromically activated layer 5 corticotectal cells) cannot be excluded
span.note: what this limits: the layer 1 sink interpretation: IT DOES NOT PROVE THAT THIS HYPOTHETICAL MODE OF ACTIVATION ACTUALLY OCCURS OR THAT DIRECT INPUT FROM THE NONPRIMARY AUDITORY THALAMUS HAD NO ROLE
span.quote: However, it does not prove that this hypothetical mode of activation actually occurs or that direct input from the nonprimary auditory thalamus had no role.

span.label: Because of that unresolved alternative, the authors advise caution in using the shell preparation
span.note: what this limits: any use of the shell preparation while the alternative is unresolved: THUS AT PRESENT IT SHOULD BE USED WITH CAUTION
span.quote: Thus at present it should be used with caution.

span.label: The pharmacological design cannot isolate the AMPA/KA contribution, since APV was never given alone
span.note: what this limits: any AMPA/KA conclusion from the pharmacology: THIS SUBTRACTIVE LOGIC CANNOT BE USED TO IMPLICATE AMPA/KA RECEPTORS BECAUSE APV WAS NEVER APPLIED BY ITSELF
span.quote: This subtractive logic cannot be used to implicate AMPA/KA receptors because APV was never applied by itself.

span.label: The synaptic order of the early response is unresolved
span.note: what this limits: the synaptic order of the early response: EXACTLY HOW MANY LINKS ARE INVOLVED IN THE EARLY RESPONSE REMAINS TO BE DETERMINED
span.quote: Exactly how many links are involved in the early response remains to be determined.

span.label: A measured quantity is stated not to be comparable across studies, because its visibility depends on method and criteria.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison of IPSP amplitudes between this study and another: the authors state it is difficult to compare IPSPs across studies because the degree to which they can be observed, and their amplitudes, depends heavily on methodology and criteria
span.quote: However, it is difficult to compare IPSPs across studies because the degree to which they can be observed, and their amplitudes, depends heavily on methodology and criteria

span.label: The conventional stimulation method is stated to be possibly unreliable for the purpose it is used for.
span.note: what this limits: any result attributing a response to thalamocortical input on the basis of columnar stimulation: the authors state their MG-evoked profiles differ from those produced by conventional columnar stimulation, which may not be a reliable means of selectively activating thalamocortical inputs
span.quote: Fourth, we observed that these MG-evoked profiles, and the intracellular responses in layer 4, differ from those produced by conventional columnar stimulation, indicating that columnar stimulation may not be a reliable means of selectively activating thalamocortical inputs

span.label: Two stimulation sites are reported not to activate the same synapses, with different laminar profiles.
span.note: what this limits: any treatment of on-beam and MG stimulation as interchangeable probes: they are stated not to activate the same sets of synapses in cortex, and to evoke different laminar profiles
span.quote: These findings indicated that MG and on-beam stimuli do not activate the same sets of synapses in cortex. This conclusion was further supported by the observation that MG and on-beam stimuli evoked different laminar profiles. While the MG stimuli produced expected profiles with dominant middle layer CSD sinks, on-beam stimuli evoked profiles that were highly variable between slices and whose largest sinks rarely appeared in the middle layers

span.label: The AMPA/KA conclusion is conditional on an assumption the authors state is difficult to prove.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that AMPA/KA receptors mediate transmission at these synapses: it follows if one assumes the fast EPSP in the middle layers is a monosynaptic event, and the authors state it is difficult to prove that a response is monosynaptic
span.quote: However, if one assumes that the fast EPSP in the middle layers is a monosynaptic event, then the virtually complete suppression of the fast EPSP by CNQX (RESULTS; Fig. 5) does implicate AMPA/KA receptors in transmission at thalamocortical synapses. Although it is difficult to prove that a response is monosynaptic, the fast EPSPs and the fast field potentials were recorded at the cortical focus, which in the pharmacological experiments was confirmed to be the position with the shortest latency middle layer field potential

span.label: Whether the preparation's evoked activation resembles the intact system is stated to be undetermined.
span.note: what this limits: any inference from these evoked responses to sound-driven cortical activity: the authors state it remains to be determined whether the activation produced by MG stimulation represents a natural pattern similar to that produced by acoustic stimulation in vivo
span.quote: It remains to be determined whether or not the cortical activation (e.g., IPSP magnitude and laminar profile) produced by MG stimulation in the primary slice represents a “natural” pattern, similar to that produced by acoustic stimulation in vivo

span.label: Inhibition may be incompletely developed at the age used, indicated by the marker staining in this material.
span.note: what this limits: any absolute inhibitory strength taken from these recordings: cortical inhibitory systems are known not to be fully developed in juvenile rodents, and the modest cortical PV labeling observed here is stated to indicate it
span.quote: For example, it is known that some aspects of cortical inhibitory systems are not fully developed in juvenile rodents (e.g., Dunning et al. 1999; Luhmann and Prince 1991; reviewed in Sutor and Luhmann 1995). In fact, this was indicated by the relatively modest cortical PV labeling observed here; PV is a marker for a class of cortical inhibitory neurons and is expressed at much higher levels in the adult mouse ACx

span.label: on-beam and MG-evoked IPSPs compared DIRECTLY WITHIN THE SAME SLICES rather than across the preparation
span.note: eliminates: preparation-dependent differences - slice health, cutting angle, anything that varies between preparations and would otherwise be read as a difference between the two pathways
span.quote: To control for these potential preparation-dependent effects, we directly compared on-beamand MG-evoked IPSPs within the same slices.

span.label: a re-analysis restricted to the SEVEN CELLS in which MG-evoked EPSPs were at least as strong as on-beam EPSPs
span.note: eliminates: weaker MG excitation as the explanation of weaker MG inhibition - if the thalamic pathway simply drove the slice less hard, smaller IPSPs would follow with no difference in inhibition itself
span.quote: To control for this potential problem, we separately compared IPSPs for the seven cells in which EPSPs evoked by MG stimulation were equal to, or stronger than, on-beam EPSPs

span.label: columnar stimulation
span.quote: Fourth, we observed that these MG-evoked profiles, and the intracellular responses in layer 4, differ from those produced by conventional columnar stimulation, indicating that columnar stimulation may not be a reliable means of selectively activating thalamocortical inputs

span.label: thalamocortical inputs
span.quote: Fourth, we observed that these MG-evoked profiles, and the intracellular responses in layer 4, differ from those produced by conventional columnar stimulation, indicating that columnar stimulation may not be a reliable means of selectively activating thalamocortical inputs

span.label: MG stimuli
span.quote: These findings indicated that MG and on-beam stimuli do not activate the same sets of synapses in cortex. This conclusion was further supported by the observation that MG and on-beam stimuli evoked different laminar profiles. While the MG stimuli produced expected profiles with dominant middle layer CSD sinks, on-beam stimuli evoked profiles that were highly variable between slices and whose largest sinks rarely appeared in the middle layers

span.label: on-beam stimuli
span.quote: These findings indicated that MG and on-beam stimuli do not activate the same sets of synapses in cortex. This conclusion was further supported by the observation that MG and on-beam stimuli evoked different laminar profiles. While the MG stimuli produced expected profiles with dominant middle layer CSD sinks, on-beam stimuli evoked profiles that were highly variable between slices and whose largest sinks rarely appeared in the middle layers

span.label: IPSPs
span.quote: if the IPSPs had been the result of direct inhibitory projections from the thalamus, then antagonism of AMPA/KA receptors could not have blocked them. Instead, it is likely that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical inhibitory interneurons to fire and those interneurons synapsed on the recorded cells, producing the IPSPs

span.label: excitatory thalamic projections
span.quote: if the IPSPs had been the result of direct inhibitory projections from the thalamus, then antagonism of AMPA/KA receptors could not have blocked them. Instead, it is likely that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical inhibitory interneurons to fire and those interneurons synapsed on the recorded cells, producing the IPSPs

span.label: cortical inhibitory interneurons
span.quote: if the IPSPs had been the result of direct inhibitory projections from the thalamus, then antagonism of AMPA/KA receptors could not have blocked them. Instead, it is likely that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical inhibitory interneurons to fire and those interneurons synapsed on the recorded cells, producing the IPSPs

span.label: an IPSP amplitude, across papers - NOT A COMPARABLE QUANTITY: whether an IPSP can be observed at all, and how large it is, depends heavily on methodology and criteria, so the same named measurement in two studies is two measurements and the authors state the comparison is difficult
span.quote: However, it is difficult to compare IPSPs across studies because the degree to which they can be observed, and their amplitudes, depends heavily on methodology and criteria

span.label: columnar (on-beam) stimulation - NOT A SELECTIVE THALAMOCORTICAL PROBE: it is used to activate thalamocortical inputs, and the authors state it may not be a reliable means of doing so selectively, because MG and on-beam stimuli do not activate the same sets of synapses
span.quote: Fourth, we observed that these MG-evoked profiles, and the intracellular responses in layer 4, differ from those produced by conventional columnar stimulation, indicating that columnar stimulation may not be a reliable means of selectively activating thalamocortical inputs

span.label: the AMPA/KA finding - HELD UP BY AN ASSUMPTION, NOT A CONTROL: the subtractive logic could not be used because APV was never applied alone, so the conclusion follows only if the fast EPSP is a monosynaptic event, which the authors state is difficult to prove
span.quote: However, if one assumes that the fast EPSP in the middle layers is a monosynaptic event, then the virtually complete suppression of the fast EPSP by CNQX (RESULTS; Fig. 5) does implicate AMPA/KA receptors in transmission at thalamocortical synapses. Although it is difficult to prove that a response is monosynaptic, the fast EPSPs and the fast field potentials were recorded at the cortical focus, which in the pharmacological experiments was confirmed to be the position with the shortest latency middle layer field potential

span.label: the early IPSPs - CORTICAL IN ROUTE, INFERRED FROM A BLOCKER RATHER THAN FROM THE RESPONSE: a direct inhibitory thalamic projection is ruled out because an AMPA/KA antagonist blocked them, and the remaining account is that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical interneurons which then synapsed on the recorded cells; the paper states this as likely, not as shown
span.quote: if the IPSPs had been the result of direct inhibitory projections from the thalamus, then antagonism of AMPA/KA receptors could not have blocked them. Instead, it is likely that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical inhibitory interneurons to fire and those interneurons synapsed on the recorded cells, producing the IPSPs

span.label: builds-on → Agmon and Connors (1991) somatosensory thalamocortical slice preparation
span.quote: To address similar problems in the somatosensory system, Agmon and Connors (1991) developed a slice preparation that maintained connections from the ventrobasal complex to barrel cortex.

span.label: extends → Metherate and Cruikshank (1999), the authors' own initial feasibility study in rat and mouse slices
span.quote: In initial studies using slices from rat and mouse, we demonstrated the likely feasibility of such a preparation by showing that stimulation within the thalamus or thalamocortical pathway could elicit cortical responses (Metherate and Cruikshank 1999).

span.label: builds-on → Barth and MacDonald (1996) finding that nonlemniscal stimulation evokes cortical gamma band activity
span.quote: These observations are broadly consistent with the finding by Barth and colleagues that stimuli presumed to activate nonlemniscal pathways evoke cortical gamma band activity whereas lemniscal stimulation does not (Barth and MacDonald 1996).

span.label: MG stimuli —contrasted-with→ on-beam stimuli
span.note: differs in: which synapses they activate, and the laminar profile they evoke · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: These findings indicated that MG and on-beam stimuli do not activate the same sets of synapses in cortex. This conclusion was further supported by the observation that MG and on-beam stimuli evoked different laminar profiles. While the MG stimuli produced expected profiles with dominant middle layer CSD sinks, on-beam stimuli evoked profiles that were highly variable between slices and whose largest sinks rarely appeared in the middle layers

span.label: cortical inhibitory interneurons —causes→ IPSPs
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.8
span.quote: if the IPSPs had been the result of direct inhibitory projections from the thalamus, then antagonism of AMPA/KA receptors could not have blocked them. Instead, it is likely that excitatory thalamic projections drove cortical inhibitory interneurons to fire and those interneurons synapsed on the recorded cells, producing the IPSPs

span.label: A mouse brain slice can be cut in a near-horizontal plane that preserves a functionally intact thalamocortical pathway from the ventral medial geniculate to auditory cortex.
span.quote: The major finding of this study is that an in vitro preparation can be obtained from the mouse brain that contains functionally intact thalamocortical connections from the MGv to the ACx.

span.label: Auditory thalamocortical transmission is carried by both AMPA/kainate and NMDA glutamate receptors.
span.quote: A second major finding is that auditory thalamocortical transmission involves both AMPA and NMDA types of glutamate receptors.

span.label: Every primary slice analysed showed a dominant current sink in cortical layers 3-4 after medial geniculate stimulation.
span.quote: Thus Fig. 3B shows that all 22 slices had a dominant sink in layers 3– 4.

span.label: Responses evoked by thalamic stimulation differ from those evoked by conventional columnar (white matter/layer 6) stimulation, so columnar stimulation is not a reliable proxy for thalamocortical activation.
span.quote: Fourth, we observed that these MG-evoked profiles, and the intracellular responses in layer 4, differ from those produced by conventional columnar stimulation, indicating that columnar stimulation may not be a reliable means of selectively activating thalamocortical inputs.

span.label: A second, more ventral 'shell' slice was introduced in which subcortical stimulation selectively activates synapses in superficial layer 1 of temporal cortex.
span.quote: Finally, a second in vitro preparation (the shell slice) is presented in which subcortical stimulation appears to selectively activate synapses in superficial layer 1 of temporal cortex.

span.label: Control tracing from the inferior colliculus confirmed that layer 5 corticotectal axons pass through the shell stimulation site, providing an alternative route for the layer 1 response.
span.quote: These data confirm the hypothesis that axons belonging to layer 5 cortico-tectal cells project through the shell stimulation region on their way to the inferior colliculus.

span.label: primary slice / shell slice
span.quote: The dorsal-most of these will be referred to as the “primary slice,” and the more ventral will be called the “shell slice” (Fig. 1).

span.label: on-beam stimulation
span.quote: This conventional white matter/layer 6 stimulation will be referred to as “on-beam” stimulation. Here we compared responses in primary slices evoked by MG and on-beam stimulation and found clear differences between them

span.label: early response
span.quote: Intracellular responses to MG stimulation typically began with a short-latency depolarizing potential that will be referred to as the “early response.”

span.label: late responses
span.quote: These long duration, presumed polysynaptic responses, will hereafter be referred to as the “late responses.”

span.label: stimulation site (medial geniculate versus on-beam white matter/layer 6)
span.term: stimulation site (medial geniculate versus on-beam white matter/layer 6)
span.quote: Here we compared responses in primary slices evoked by MG and on-beam stimulation and found clear differences between them relating to IPSP strengths and CSD distributions.

span.quote: To determine the laminar locations of current sinks and sources, onedimensional current source density (CSD) analysis was performed (Agmon and Connors 1991; Johnston and Wu 1995; Mitzdorf 1985).
